title: Seamless replica failover with stream snapshotting and adaptive traffic shaping
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Problem: Hosted API active-active gateways must fail over individual streaming sessions and short-lived conversational sessions across replicas/regions without user-visible truncation or large latency spikes. Current graceful drain causes lost token continuity for a subset of long-lived streaming sessions and unpredictable p99 latency increases during regional traffic drains.

Goal: Implement a replica-level snapshot + delta-replay approach to migrate session state (KV cache pointers, session checkpoints, partial response buffers) and pair that with adaptive traffic shaping so traffic shifts maintain SLOs. Provide circuit-breaker behavior and load-shedding policies that preserve high-priority sessions while minimizing customer visible errors.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change model checkpoint formats or introduce cross-model state merging. It does not implement cross-region synchronization of persistent storage outside the transient session handoff flow.
acceptance_criteria: Per-session failover succeeds for > 95% of active streams with no more than a single resumed chunk delivery delay (max additional 300ms) during cross-region handoff in lab tests.
Failover runbook triggers when regional capacity drop causes routing to shift >= 20% of traffic and restores within SLOs for p50/p95/p99 latency targets.
Circuit-breaker config prevents cascading overload: when downstream error rate > 1.0% across replicas, traffic is routed to fallback small-variant with preserved token continuity in > 90% of cases.
Metrics and dashboards for kv_sync_lag_ms, stream_checkpoint_success_rate, active_streams_handled_by_replica, and cross_region_handoff_rate are available in Console > Resilience > Failover.
Integration tests exercise snapshot creation, transfer, and resume for 1s, 10s, 60s, and 10-minute sessions with encoded KV sizes representative of production (up to 1.2 MB per session).
implementation_notes:
Design: 1) Session snapshot producer: at configurable quanta (first-chunk, steady-state every 5s, and immediate pre-drain checkpoint) serializer writes a lightweight snapshot of session head, last event token, and compressed KV diff. 2) Snapshot transfer: use regional gossip channel with authenticated transport (mTLS) and push to candidate replicas; if cross-region, push to dedicated failover endpoint in target region. 3) Snapshot consumer: verify snapshot signature, warm KV cache pointers, allocate session slot, and resume stream from last event token. 4) Adaptive traffic shaper: when shifting N% of traffic, shape ramp to maintain per-replica CPU/GPU utilization below 80% and keep p99 < 400ms by controlling batching window and per-connection concurrency. 5) Circuit breakers: implement per-replica and cluster-level CBs with sliding window error-rate detection and backoff policy that re-routes to prioritized fallback variants.

Trade-offs: snapshotting increases transient network and CPU usage; we limit snapshot frequency and compress diffs. A strong consistency handoff would be slower; we accept eventual KV rehydration for low-priority sessions.

Backward compatibility: snapshots include schema_version; older replicas ignore extended fields and perform best-effort resume.
observability_requirements: New metrics: token_resume_latency_ms (histogram), kv_snapshot_size_bytes, kv_sync_lag_ms (gauge), snapshot_transfer_success_ratio (rolling 5m), active_sessions_awaiting_resume (gauge). Add dashboard with alerting rules: kv_sync_lag_ms > 2000ms for 5m -> P1. High error-rate during ramp (>1% for 2m) -> automated rollback of shift. Expose sample traces for resumed streams in Console to show resume boundary spans and end-to-end latency.
test_plan: Unit tests for serializer/deserializer and signature verification. Integration tests in dev cluster that simulate region outage and verify resume behavior for 1k synthetic sessions of mixed sizes. Chaos test: kill replica during transfer to verify fallback is not dropping sessions. Load test: ramp to production-equivalent load and measure p95/p99 during a 30% cross-region shift. Canary: enable snapshotting in a single region with 2% of traffic before global rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag default-off. 2) Enable in region-us-east-1 with 2% traffic for 48h (canary). 3) If metrics stable, increase to 20% over 6h with automated checks. 4) Enable cross-region for non-critical customers only. 5) Full rollout after 2 weeks and post-mortem review. Include an automated abort on p99 or error-rate regression beyond thresholds.
runbook_snippet: When a regional outage is detected: 1) Validate region outage via multi-source telemetry. 2) Trigger controlled ramp: routing controller sets shift_goal to N% and starts snapshot pre-drain for top 1k longest-lived sessions. 3) Monitor kv_sync_lag_ms and snapshot_transfer_success_ratio; if success_ratio < 90% after ramp, revert and increase snapshot compression for retries. 4) If CB opens for a replica, escalate to on-call and switch traffic to next-priority replica pool. 5) After failover, run post-incident check to claim final metrics and archive snapshots for 72h for debugging.
open_questions: What is the maximum acceptable snapshot payload per session to avoid saturating inter-region links? (suggestion: 1.5MB ceiling)
Should low-priority sessions be resumed lazily (background) to reduce immediate ramp pressure?
Do we need customer-configurable failover tiers (gold/silver/bronze) wired into routing policies?
decisions: Use pre-drain checkpoint + steady-state deltas rather than continuous stream mirroring to reduce bandwidth.
Snapshots will be signed and compressed; transfer uses existing mTLS gossip channels with explicit routing headers for region preference.
Circuit-breaker threshold: initial error-rate threshold set to 1.0% over 60s sliding window; revisit after canary.
Load-shedding policy: prefer dropping lowest-priority streaming connections (based on customer tier and session age) before dropping synchronous API requests.
